newsitem.title: GERMANY: German rubber industry hopes to raise 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: German rubber industry hopes to raise 1997 sales.

text.p: German manufacturers of rubber products expect to increase sales by 2.5 to three percent in 1997 after a 1.7 percent rise to 16.42 billion marks in 1996, a statement from industry association WDK said.
The statement cited improved conditions in the key consuming industries such as the automotive sector, which takes 70 percent of all rubber products, but excluded construction and mining.
The relatively smaller sales increase in 1996 was attributed to sluggish demand for technical rubber products, where sales declined by 0.9 percent to 7.01 billion.
Tyre sales on the other hand gained 3.7 percent at 9.42 billion marks. The figures were rounded.
Exports in both product groups improved by 7.3 and 6.6 percent respectively.
The 1996 tonnage was down by 0.5 percent at 1.59 million tonnes of which tyres represented 1.07 million (up 0.7 percent) and techical products 516,000 tonnes (down three percent).
The industry planned investments totalling 900 million marks this year, mostly in restructuring and modernisation, the statement also said.
Some domestic jobs and manufacturing capacity would be moved abroad as the industry planned to follow its car industry customers to countries with a lower cost structure.
